correctness.rationale: For each used color, summing the exact majority inequalities over the partite support forces its color-class size to be at least half the graph order. Thus at most two colors can occur. Equality with two colors forces support on every part and equality in every local inequality, hence exact half-splitting in each part and even part sizes. The converse construction and product count are immediate and were independently stress-tested by exhaustive neighborhood checks through order 8.

value.rationale: The initiating paper treats complete bipartite graphs as a basic exact family. Extending this to every complete multipartite graph yields a sharp parity criterion, proves a global two-color ceiling, and classifies and counts every optimum two-coloring on a broad classical graph family. The result is structural and reusable rather than a routine single-parameter computation.
